title: Optical Holder for in-situ Pulsed Laser Deposition and Dewetting of Metal Films
content: In situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) experiments offer invaluable insights into material systems by enabling real-time observation of dynamic processes and transformations with nanoscale resolution. To accomplish this, innovative holder designs have been developed to apply additional stimuli to samples, including heating/cooling, straining, and electrical bias. Despite these advances, in situ dynamics of certain technologically relevant processes remain difficult to access inside the TEM, for example extreme temperature processing, material ablation, and solid-state deposition.
